case_name: Aabira Mukherjee vs Swapna Roy & Ors
facts_of_case: The plaintiff claims that the deed of settlement by trust dated October 6, 1993 is null and void. The plaintiff also seeks a decree declaring itself as the sole and absolute owner of premises No. 46, Mahendra Sarkar Street, Kolkata 700012.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu widow's right to maintenance is a pre-existing right.
legal_principles.held: He submits that in terms of Compromise Decree and the terms of Settlement, the premises was given to Durga Rani Ghosh for her use, enjoyment through her life.
cited_cases: V. Tulasamma & Ors. Vs. Sesha Reddy (Dead) by L.Rs., (1977) 3 SCC 99
Jupudy Pardha Sarathy Vs. Pentapati Rama Krishna & Ors., (2016) 2 SCC 56

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu female acquiring property at partition or in lieu of right of maintenance has a pre-existing right.
legal_principles.held: He submits that before the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 came into force, the Hindu Married Women's Right to Separate Maintenance and Residence Act, 1946 was enacted to give statutory recognition of such right
cited_cases: V. Tulasamma & Ors. Vs. Sesha Reddy (Dead) by L.Rs., (1977) 3 SCC 99
Jupudy Pardha Sarathy Vs. Pentapati Rama Krishna & Ors., (2016) 2 SCC 56

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu widow has a personal obligation to maintain her husband, and if he is possessed of properties, she is entitled to a right to be maintained out of such properties.
legal_principles.held: He submits that under the Hindu Law, the husband has got a personal obligation to maintain his wife and if he is possessed of properties then his wife is entitled to a right to be maintained out of such properties
cited_cases: Jupudy Pardha Sarathy Vs. Pentapati Rama Krishna & Ors., (2016) 2 SCC 56

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu female acquiring property at partition or in lieu of right of maintenance has a pre-existing right, and such an acquisition would not be within the scope and ambit of sub-section (2) even if the instrument, decree, order or award allotting the property prescribes a restricted estate in the property.
legal_principles.held: He submits that the property is acquired by a Hindu female at the partition or in lieu of right of maintenance, it is in virtue of a pre-existing right and such an acquisition would not be within the scope and ambit of sub-section (2), even if the instrument, decree, order or award allotting the property prescribes a restricted estate in the property
cited_cases: V. Tulasamma & Ors. Vs. Sesha Reddy (Dead) by L.Rs., (1977) 3 SCC 99

outcome.final_order: The court granted the plaintiff's relief claims, including declaring the deed of settlement by trust null and void, and directing the defendants to deliver up the said deed.

use_for_drafting: representing clients in property ownership disputes
